message.content:
Write two node:test files for a meeting-room booking server: `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/api-routes.test.mjs` (routing, 404/405, content types, page serving) and `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/api-list.test.mjs` (GET list sorting, ?date filter, DELETE id rules).

RULES: ES module, Node built-ins only (`node:test`, `node:assert/strict`, fs, path). Use helpers in `/root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/test/helpers/server.mjs` (read it first: startServer({cwd, env}), request(port,{method,path,headers,body}) — path is sent raw, rawRequest(port, bytes), postBooking, getBookings, writeStore, makeTmpDir, booking(overrides), ROOT, JSON_TYPE). Do NOT edit helpers, server.mjs or public/. Exact equality on all spec values (strictEqual/deepStrictEqual) — never prefix/regex. One server per file (or per describe) started in before(), stopped in after(), tmp dir removed. No console.log. Each file ≤ 400 lines, functions < 50 lines; table-driven tests welcome. Run `cd /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2 && node --test test/api-routes.test.mjs test/api-list.test.mjs` until passing. If a test fails on the real server and the spec clearly says otherwise, do NOT weaken it: keep it and report it with repro.

Spec excerpt (full: /root/bench-runs/h4-b3949ce2/.team/notes/spec.md):
- Rooms fixed: Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos in that order. Booking = exactly keys id(number), room, title, date, start, end.
- Path = request target up to first `?`. Routes compare byte for byte: no percent-decoding, no dot-segment/slash/case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms`, `/api/bookings/` match none. Query ignored unless stated, decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)`.
- GET /api/rooms → 200 {"rooms":["Aurora","Borealis","Cosmos"]}.
- GET /api/bookings → 200 {"bookings":[...]} every booking sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. With a `date` param (`params.has('date')`; `?date` with no `=` counts with empty value), its value is params.get('date') (first when repeated) and only bookings on that date are returned; a value not a valid date (YYYY-MM-DD, ASCII digits, real day 2000-01-01..2099-12-31, Feb 29 in years divisible by 4; empty included) → 400 {"error":"date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date"}. Other params ignored.
- DELETE /api/bookings/<id>: every path `/api/bookings/` + non-empty <id> with no `/` is this route whatever <id> is. 204 empty body, booking gone. <id> not a positive integer in ASCII digits without leading zero, or unknown → 404 {"error":"booking not found"}.
- GET / and GET /app.js serve the page: `/` → 200 Content-Type exactly `text/html; charset=utf-8`, body = public/index.html; `/app.js` → 200 `text/javascript; charset=utf-8`, body = public/app.js.
- Any other path: 404 {"error":"not found"} whatever the method, including paths starting with `/api/bookings/` whose rest is empty or holds a `/` (`/api/bookings/`, `/api/bookings/1/`).
- Known path with a method not listed (HEAD and OPTIONS included) → 405 {"error":"method not allowed"}. E.g. GET /api/bookings/abc is 405.
- Every reply with a body other than page and script has Content-Type exactly `application/json; charset=utf-8`. Error reply is exactly {"error": msg} (deepStrictEqual, single key).

api-routes tests:
- GET /api/rooms exact body + content type; `/api/rooms?x=1` and `/api/rooms?` also 200.
- 404 `not found` table for every method GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, OPTIONS on paths: /api/%62ookings, /api/./rooms, /API/rooms, /api/Bookings, /api/bookings/, /api/bookings/1/, /api/bookings//, /api/bookings/1/2, /api/rooms/, /api, /api/, /index.html, /app.js/, /APP.JS, //api/rooms, /api/bookings%2F1, /nope. For HEAD on these: status 404 (no body expected). For POST include a valid JSON booking body with Content-Type application/json (still 404). Also rawRequest `OPTIONS * HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n` → status line 404 (parse status from raw text's first line) — if Node itself answers this differently, report it rather than delete.
- 405 table: /api/rooms: POST PUT DELETE PATCH HEAD OPTIONS; /api/bookings: PUT DELETE PATCH HEAD OPTIONS; /api/bookings/1, /api/bookings/abc, /api/bookings/%2F: GET POST PUT PATCH HEAD OPTIONS; / and /app.js: POST PUT DELETE PATCH HEAD OPTIONS. Body exact (HEAD: status 405, content-type header exact, text ''). POST /api/bookings/1 with a valid JSON body → 405. POST /api/rooms with valid JSON → 405.
- Page: GET / bytes === readFileSync(ROOT/public/index.html) (compare Buffer/text exactly) and content-type exact; GET /app.js same with app.js; GET /?a=b and /app.js?v=1 also serve them.
- DELETE /api/bookings/%2F → 404 `booking not found` (route matched, id invalid) — distinguishes from `not found`.

api-list tests (fresh server; seed via POST in this scrambled insertion order, all distinct-non-overlapping):
 1 Cosmos 2026-11-04 09:00-10:00; 2 Aurora 2026-11-04 08:00-09:00; 3 Borealis 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00; 4 Cosmos 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00; 5 Borealis 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00; 6 Aurora 2026-11-03 09:00-10:00; 7 Aurora 2026-10-31 23:00-23:59; 8 Aurora 2026-12-01 00:00-00:30; 9 Aurora 2025-12-31 12:00-13:00; 10 Cosmos 2026-11-05 08:00-12:00; 11 Borealis 2026-11-05 08:30-09:00; 12 Aurora 2026-11-05 09:00-09:30.
 Expected GET order of ids: 9,7,6,5,4,3,2,1,10,11,12,8 — assert deepStrictEqual on the full booking objects (exact keys and values).
- Filter: ?date=2026-11-03 → ids [6,5,4,3]; ?date=2026-11-03&date=2026-11-04 → first; ?date=bad&date=2026-11-03 → 400; ?x=1&date=2026-11-04 → [2,1]; ?&date=2026-11-03 ok; ?date=%32026-11-03 and ?date=2026%2D11%2D03 → filter (decoded); ?date=2024-02-29, ?date=2000-01-01, ?date=2099-12-31 → 200 []; 400 table: ?date, ?date=, ?date=2026-02-30, ?date=2023-02-29, ?date=1999-12-31, ?date=2100-01-01, ?date=2026-11-3, ?date=+2026-11-03 (decodes to leading space), ?date=2026-11-03+ , ?date=%202026-11-03, ?date=2026-11-03?x, ?date=2026-13-01, ?date=%D9%A2%D9%A0%D9%A2%D9%A6-%D9%A1%D9%A1-%D9%A0%D9%A3 (Arabic-Indic digits). Ignored (→ all 12): ?Date=bad, ?dates=bad, ?a=1?date=bad (query is `a=1?date=bad`), ?x. 400 bodies exact + content type.
- DELETE id rules (after seeding): ids 01, 0, 00, -1, 1.0, %31, +1, %201, 1e0, 0x1, abc, 99, 13 (next id, unused), 18446744073709551617 → each 404 {error:'booking not found'}; afterwards GET still has all 12. DELETE /api/bookings/1 → 204, text '' ; GET lacks 1; DELETE /api/bookings/1 again → 404 booking not found. DELETE /api/bookings/2?x=1 → 204 (query ignored). DELETE /api/bookings/3/ → 404 `not found` and 3 still present. GET /api/bookings/4 → 405, 4 still present.

Final message: test counts, pass/fail, failing-on-real-code tests with repro, line counts.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.
